Rename chromosome identifiers in BAM, BED, or BigWig files

Source: R/rename_chromosomes.R
HORIZON_rename_chromosomes.Rd

Scans the sample output directory for files whose names end with file_suffix, then renames chromosome identifiers according to chr_map. Useful when aligning to a T2T or NCBI-style reference that uses accession-style names (e.g. NC_060925.1) rather than conventional UCSC-style names (e.g. chr1).

Usage

HORIZON_rename_chromosomes(
  sample_sheet,
  sample_id,
  chr_map,
  file_suffix,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  rename_suffix = "_chrrenamed"
)

Arguments

sample_sheet

Validated sample sheet data.frame from HORIZON_validate_sample_sheet.

sample_id

Character. Sample ID to process.

chr_map

Named character vector (names = old chromosome identifiers, values = new names), a path to a two-column tab-separated file (no header; column 1 = old, column 2 = new), or "T2TCHM13" for the built-in T2T-CHM13v2.0 NCBI-to-UCSC map (NC_060925.1 \(\to\) chr1, ...).

file_suffix

Character. Files whose basenames end with this string (case-sensitive) are processed. Use a specific trailing fragment to target one file (e.g. "RPKM.bw", "_sorted.bam") or a broader ending to match several files of the same type. The file type (bam, bed, or bw) is derived from the extension of file_suffix and determines the renaming strategy.

overwrite

Logical. If TRUE, the renamed file replaces the original (via a safe temp-file swap). Default FALSE: a new file is written with rename_suffix inserted before the extension.

rename_suffix

Character. String appended to the base name before the extension when overwrite = FALSE. Default "_chrrenamed".

Value

Character vector of output file paths, invisibly.

Details

BAM: Requires samtools in the conda environment registered via HORIZON_set_conda_env (only the header @SQ SN: fields are rewritten; the binary read data is unchanged). The output BAM is automatically re-indexed.

BigWig: Requires the Bioconductor package rtracklayer. Install via BiocManager::install("rtracklayer").

BED: Handled in pure R (no extra dependencies).
